inputs.label: Model size
inputs.tooltip: How many numbers (weights) the model learns. A 7B model has 7 billion.

inputs.label: Training data
inputs.tooltip: How much text the model reads during training. A token is roughly three quarters of a word.

inputs.label: Number of GPUs
inputs.tooltip: How many graphics chips work on the run at once. This changes how long it takes, not what it costs.

inputs.label: Chip peak speed
inputs.tooltip: The most arithmetic one chip can do per second on paper (dense BF16, from the datasheet).

inputs.label: Chip power rating
inputs.tooltip: The power a chip is designed to draw at full load (TDP, from the datasheet).

inputs.label: GPU speed actually achieved (MFU)
inputs.tooltip: Model FLOPs utilization: the share of the chip's paper speed that real training reaches. Real runs: 30-55%. 40% is a middle guess.

inputs.label: Datacenter overhead (PUE)
inputs.tooltip: Power usage effectiveness: total building power divided by computer power. 1.2 means cooling and other overhead add 20%.

inputs.label: Electricity price
inputs.tooltip: What one kilowatt-hour costs. Default is the 2024 U.S. industrial average (EIA).

inputs.label: GPU purchase price
inputs.tooltip: What one GPU costs to buy. Default depends on the GPU and is a rough market figure.

inputs.label: Years of use before replacement
inputs.tooltip: The hardware's price is spread over this many years. Longer life means cheaper hours.

inputs.label: Resale value at end of life
inputs.tooltip: The share of the purchase price you get back when the GPU is retired.

inputs.label: Servers, network and building, as a share of GPU price
inputs.tooltip: Each GPU needs a server, network and space. Default 40% follows the repo's DGX H100 cost preset: server parts about 18% of the GPU price, rack about 5%, building power and cooling about 19%.

inputs.label: GPU power draw during training
inputs.tooltip: Training rarely pulls the full rated power. 80% is a guess; measured values are often 60-90%.

inputs.label: Extra server power (CPUs, fans, network)
inputs.tooltip: Power drawn by the rest of the server, as a share of the GPUs' own power.

H100-SXM.label: NVIDIA H100 SXM
H100-SXM.price_note: 2024 channel range $27,000-$40,000 per card; $30,000 is the middle (repo DGX H100 preset).
H100-SXM.cite: NVIDIA H100 product page, H100 SXM: BFLOAT16 Tensor Core 1,979 teraFLOPS with sparsity (dense is half, 989.4 teraFLOPS); Max TDP up to 700W; 80 GB memory.

A100-80GB-SXM.label: NVIDIA A100 80GB SXM
A100-80GB-SXM.cite: NVIDIA A100 datasheet, 80GB SXM: BFLOAT16 Tensor Core 312 TFLOPS (624 with sparsity); Max TDP SXM 400W; 80 GB memory.

training_days.label: Training time
training_days.tooltip: How long the run takes on the wall clock if every GPU works at the speed achieved.

neutral_settings.text: No extra work from re-computing results to save memory.
The optimizer's extra arithmetic is ignored.
No time lost waiting for the network (it is folded into the speed actually achieved).
No extra time waiting on memory (also folded into the speed actually achieved).
No idle time added to each step.
The cluster never breaks and no work is repeated.
This run uses the whole cluster.
No staff, maintenance, water, network or carbon cost.
Tokens per step. It cancels out of every result.

not_included: Staff, building upkeep, water, network and storage costs, failed or repeated runs, and the research that came before the final run.

accuracy.text: Checked against 27 published training runs: typically within about 22% (same as the simple rule of thumb).
